newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, snow limits new crop gains.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, snow limits new crop gains.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mixed, with heavy snows in western Kansas limiting gains in new crop contracts, traders said.
KCBT wheat futures received a late boost from fund buying in the May contract and from what the market perceived as bullish comments by USDA Secretary Dan Glickman.

Glickman told the Agriculture Outlook Conference in Washington that the U.S. farm trade relationship with the European Union was "particularly tenuous." He said the U.S. had held its fire but said "we can't hold out unilaterally forever."
Traders said this could hint at a possible resumption of the U.S. Export Enhancement Program.
Meanwhile, traders said new crop July and September contracts were subject to commercial selling because of the chance that the snows in Kansas will help improve the crop.
Traders said Cargill Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of July. But mill demand for the July calls in options was noted.
"There was flour mill buying in options, they were buying the $3.60 calls in the July for coverage," a trader said at the midsession.
The nearby March contract also gained amid short covering and the unwinding of bear spreads with bullish input from USDA's weekly export inspections.
USDA early Monday said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended Feb 20 totaled 13.946 million bushels, above trade expectations for nine to 12 million bushels.
KCBT wheat settled 1-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 4-3/4 cents higher, with March up 4-3/4 cents at $3.71-1/2.
Fund-related activity in May came from Refco, which picked up 2.6 million bushels, and Man International, which bought 1.7 million.
